title: Modular-Annihilator Parent Hamiltonians for Purified Gibbs States: Spectral Design and Controlled Approximation
authors: Changhao Yi, Jun Takahashi, Cunlu Zhou
abstract: Purified Gibbs states provide a bridge between finite-temperature physics, dissipative dynamics, and ground-state methods. In this work, we study the exact finite sum-of-squares (SoS) construction of their parent Hamiltonians and the associated Lindbladian based on modular annihilators. Given a finite set of Hermitian generators, the corresponding modular annihilators yield a frustration-free SoS representation without continuous time integrals or an explicit decomposition into Bohr-frequency sectors. The purified Gibbs state remains a common zero mode while the freedom to choose and combine the generators can be used to optimize the spectral properties of the parent Hamiltonian. For free-fermion Hamiltonians, modular transformations act linearly on Majorana operators, leading to an analytically solvable family of parent Hamiltonians parameterized by a real symmetric coefficient matrix \(S\). For the scalar-functional subclass $S=f(h)$, we show that, at fixed operator norm, the choice $S_{\mathrm{opt}}\propto 1/\sqrt{\cosh(2βh)}$ has mixing time upper bound $2\log(2N/ε)$ for any $β$, which exhibits rapid mixing and is irrelevant to the inverse temperature $β$. For interacting systems, where the modularly dressed generators are not available in closed form, we introduce a Krylov--Lanczos approximation scheme and bound the resulting ground-state error in terms of the modular-approximation error and the parent-Hamiltonian gap. Numerical results illustrate the free-fermion spectral advantage and show how the accuracy of the interacting construction depends on temperature, interaction strength, and Krylov dimension.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, exact method using modular annihilators to construct parent Hamiltonians whose ground state corresponds to a purified Gibbs state. It achieves optimal spectral properties for free-fermion models and provides a systematic approximation scheme for complex interacting systems. This advances the theoretical understanding of how finite-temperature dynamics can be mapped onto ground-state problems.
main_problem: The paper develops an exact, finite Sum-of-Squares (SoS) construction for the parent Hamiltonians associated with purified Gibbs states, bypassing continuous time integrals.
main_result: The modular-annihilator construction achieves the optimal relative spectral gap of 1 for the parent Hamiltonian, and the optimal free-fermion choice yields rapid mixing independent of inverse temperature.
method: The core method involves using modular annihilators derived from a finite set of Hermitian generators to construct the parent Hamiltonian $M_H$ such that the purified Gibbs state is its unique ground state.
model_or_system: The study focuses on purified Gibbs states ($ho_ eta$), which bridge finite-temperature physics and ground-state methods. The analysis covers free-fermion models (using Majorana operators) and general interacting systems.
key_observables: Spectral gap of the parent Hamiltonian ($	ext{Gap}(M_H)$), mixing time, and the relative spectral gap $r(\{J_a\})$.
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), interaction strength, and the dimension of the Krylov approximation.
main_assumptions: The construction assumes the algebra generated by the initial operators is unital and irreducible for the ground state to be unique. Interacting systems require the Krylov-Lanczos approximation.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general concept of purifying Gibbs states to the specific construction using modular annihilators, detailing the free-fermion case, and finally addressing the approximation techniques for general interacting systems.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, non-perturbative methods to connect thermal equilibrium states (Gibbs states) to ground-state physics via parent Hamiltonians, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems dynamics.
